absent: PCI configuration access serialization and AMD northbridge range table population
AGP bridge search, aperture validity, allocation, core-exclusion and resume handling
e820 table update synchronization and reserved-range lifecycle
APIC MMIO mapping, register layout beyond names used, and driver dispatch internals
Clock-event core registration, frequency update races, and broadcast topology handling
Microcode revision source and hardware effects behind deadline errata
Power-management timer calibration sequence and scheduler clock selection beyond native check

findings.text: Early GART check runs at boot, exits when the platform lacks GART or early PCI access is unavailable, surveys AMD northbridge functions for aperture agreement, reserves a RAM-conflicting window when requested, and disables apertures when no valid AGP window remains.

GART hole initialization disables translation before sampling each node, validates per-node windows, reuses a matching AGP window or allocates a fallback window when BIOS left none or nodes disagree, then programs a uniform window into all nodes and records resume state.

Aperture size is derived from a small order field scaled from a 32 MB base and the base value is shifted to a bus address; all nodes must agree on enable, order and base, and the resulting window must be non-empty and below the 4 GB limit or repair is required.

Translation is disabled before reprogramming because reconfiguring an enabled GART has unknown effects, and boot is aborted when a needed fallback aperture cannot be allocated because later users cannot tolerate a bad window over memory.
Memory map helper reports whether any entry of a requested type overlaps a caller supplied address interval using the global table.
Overlap scan skips entries whose type differs when a type filter is supplied and treats merely touching boundaries as non-overlapping.
Local APIC resource descriptor names a memory reservation for the local APIC with memory and busy attributes.

Boot APIC identity and mode state is held read-only after init, covering boot identifiers and version, extended NMI and destination mode selections, MMIO base, MP table address, disable and verbosity and PIC mode flags, timer C-state permission, and stored timer period.
Two small mode helpers select whether platform interrupts travel through the APIC or directly to the bootstrap processor via the IMCR configuration selector.
Local APIC boot option forces local APIC enablement on 32-bit when no value is supplied and clears deadline timer capability when the corresponding option string is present.
APIC PM timer boot option records a calibration request and marks the timestamp counter unstable through the shared no-TSC path.
Marking the TSC unstable is a one-way latch that clears the stable scheduler clock when native and flags both early and normal TSC clock sources as unstable.
The APIC is considered accessible when extended mode is active or an MMIO base has been assigned.
Local APIC countdown conversion uses divisor sixteen and deadline conversion uses divisor eight.
Discrete 82489DX timer base divider uses value two placed at bit eighteen of the timer entry.

Integrated APIC detection decodes the version register; recent AMD and all Hygon are treated as modern while other systems require a version threshold; discrete parts report a fixed small LVT count while integrated parts decode the count from hardware.
Interprocessor command register issue is protected by local interrupt masking across the destination and command halves, while the read path combines both halves into one 64-bit value.
APIC disable during init replaces the active driver with a no-operation driver.

Local timer entry programming selects periodic, one-shot, or deadline behavior from caller mode plus CPU capability, applies a discrete divider quirk and optional masking, orders deadline entry with a fence, otherwise selects divide-by-sixteen and loads an initial count only for periodic mode.

Extended LVT offset assignment uses atomic compare-exchange reservation and allows replacement only when the old entry was masked, the new request is masked, or the unmasked payload is unchanged; out-of-range offsets fail.
Extended LVT setup combines mask, message type and vector, rejects cross-CPU reservation mismatch and incompatible same-CPU reuse as firmware bugs, then writes the hardware register.

Countdown next-event writes the supplied delta to the initial count while the deadline variant adds a scaled delta to the current TSC and writes the deadline register; shutdown masks the timer entry and clears active counting state with extra zeroing for errata; dummy broadcast devices ignore changes.
Periodic and one-shot transitions share a helper that programs the timer entry with the stored period and enabled interrupts while ignoring dummy devices.

Default LAPIC clock-event template advertises periodic, one-shot, C3-stop and dummy capabilities with 32-bit shift, rating one hundred, and callbacks for shutdown, periodic, one-shot, next-event and broadcast; per-CPU instances hold instantiated state.

Per-CPU timer setup clones the template, binds it to the current CPU, removes C3-stop and raises preference on always-running systems, and switches deadline-capable CPUs to a deadline device with coupled TSC identity and frequency derived from the TSC rate.
Timer broadcast forwards the local timer vector as an interprocessor interrupt to the supplied mask on SMP builds.

Deadline timer use is gated by CPU support, virtualization exceptions, and a microcode revision table for listed Intel families; insufficient microcode is reported as a firmware bug and the capability is cleared.
CPU table matcher returns the first entry whose vendor, family, model, stepping, platform, feature and type constraints all accept the boot CPU, else no match.
TSC frequency change is propagated to every CPU, where deadline-capable timer devices recompute their event frequency from the current TSC rate.
